answer: A tundra crossing keeps one heated haven per agent, each with a hand-built wind vane and a snow stake outside the door. Each epoch the agent reads the zephyr at the vane, measures the snow line on the stake, and files both numbers before the crossing bell. The next haven down the trail checks the reading against its own wind, since a real gust crosses the tundra in a known order and a copied number arrives out of sequence. A thousand fake names need a thousand real havens, each with a vane that turns in the wind and a reading filed before the bell.
